definitions.explanation: The yellowish-white fluid that forms at the site of an infection, consisting of dead white blood cells, bacteria, and tissue debris.
Used figuratively to refer to deep-seated corruption, problems, or dysfunction within an organization or system that needs to be exposed and dealt with.

examples.japanese: {傷口|きずぐち}から{膿|うみ}が{出|で}ている。
examples.english: Pus is coming out of the wound.

examples.japanese: {膿|うみ}を{出|だ}してから{消毒|しょうどく}した。
examples.english: I disinfected it after draining the pus.

examples.japanese: {歯茎|はぐき}が{腫|は}れて{膿|うみ}がたまっていた。
examples.english: My gums were swollen and pus had accumulated.

examples.japanese: {組織|そしき}の{膿|うみ}を{出|だ}し{切|き}る。
examples.english: To root out all the corruption in the organization.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{膿|うみ}を{出|だ}す{改革|かいかく}が{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: Reforms that root out years of accumulated rot are needed.

examples.japanese: {不祥事|ふしょうじ}をきっかけに、{会社|かいしゃ}の{膿|うみ}が{次々|つぎつぎ}と{明|あき}らかになった。
examples.english: Triggered by the scandal, the company's deep-seated corruption was exposed one after another.

notes:
A basic medical term that is also widely used as a powerful metaphor for corruption and systemic problems.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {膿|うみ}が{出|で}る: pus comes out
- {膿|うみ}を{出|だ}す: to drain pus; to root out corruption
- {膿|うみ}がたまる: pus accumulates; problems fester
- {膿|うみ}を{出|だ}し{切|き}る: to completely drain the pus/corruption

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Do not confuse with {海|うみ} (sea, ocean), which has the same pronunciation.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {化膿|かのう}: suppuration, festering — the medical process of pus formation
- {腐敗|ふはい}: corruption, decay — used figuratively for organizational corruption
